examples: See every paired computer's load, memory and disk beside the compute it keeps free for its owner.
Make another computer the Pack alpha, and see at once when two computers disagree about which one it is.
Stop a paired computer from hosting more than two agents, from that computer or from this one.
how_to: Open the pack row in the menu (press h with the menu focused). The computers tab lists every computer once, this computer first: its name, the alpha badge, a green computer icon for this computer, a two-computers icon for the link (green while the computer answers, grey within about half a minute of it going quiet), model and cores, cpu, memory and disk as segmented meters, and the installed tools row.

A meter is 20 cells outlined in a hairline: green under 75 percent, amber from 75, coral from 90. The compute reserve shows as a hatched zone at the top end of the bar. cpu is the 1 minute load average over the cores, so 5/10 is load 5 on 10 cores.

Press make alpha next to a computer's name, on the computer that is alpha now, to hand alpha to another computer; every paired computer follows within seconds, because each one accepts only a change signed by the alpha it follows. Pressed on any other computer it changes only that computer, and the others raise a refused pack change alert offering to follow it there.

On the work tab: a status strip (the alpha, computers online, whether this computer follows it) and the follow the alpha switch with a more disclosure; placement with spread work across the pack and enhanced placement (changed on alpha; elsewhere the change is refused as not alpha), whose connection and model pickers appear inline while it is on and state the default in the field; per computer, its real compute reserve and restrictions as chips with edit opening the editor in place; and move a project or company, which needs both the project and the target computer before the move button enables.
Restrictions on another computer can only be tightened from here; that computer's own owner loosens them.
On the logins tab: switch the credential relay on per Claude account, and this computer's own may receive credentials switch.

On a project's page, open transport... to set air-gap, see which github account the project uses and where that came from, pick one of the logged-in accounts, see how a replica would get the code, and publish a private repo for a folder with no remote.
A session or Swarm agent running on another computer wears that computer's name as a small badge on the Swarm page and in its chat header.
The ssh tab holds ssh-only machines and the pairing tools.
name: Pack machines
summary: every paired computer in the Pack with live load, the one alpha marked, the compute reserve kept for the owner, and restrictions each computer enforces on its own peers.
